paper.title: Joint Optimization and Variable Selection of High-dimensional Gaussian Processes

settings.name_in_paper: Variable selection of a high-dimensional GP sample depending on few active variables (HDS)
unmapped: goal is to identify the set A of active coordinates of f on [-1,1]^D (extrinsic dimension D, d=|A| active)
f depends only on an unknown subset of d active variables; kernel is SE over active coordinates only, with known bandwidth b and self-variance sigma_s^2
settings.definition_quote: Let f : [−1, 1]^D → R be a fixed, but unknown function... We assume that this function depends only on a subset of the domain variables, which we call the active variables... we assume that it is a sample from a Gaussian Process ... with zero mean and a squared-exponential kernel K... y_t = f(x_t) + ε_t where ε_t are i.i.d. normal random variables with zero mean and variance σ^2 > 0 (assumed known)

settings.name_in_paper: Joint variable selection and GP optimization (cumulative regret)
unmapped: f on [-1,1]^D depends only on d unknown active variables; SE kernel over active coordinates with known bandwidth b and self-variance sigma_s^2
the learner knows the number of active variables d (used in beta_t)
per-round regret bounded by known C_0
settings.definition_quote:
We evaluate any candidate algorithm in
PT
terms of its regret, RT = t=1 [f (x∗ ) − f (xt )].

algorithms.name: Hierarchical Diagonal Sampling (HDS) with generic test
HDS with non-sequential Finite Difference Test (HDS-FDT)
HDS-FDT followed by GP-UCB on active variables

symbols.alpha_err: false positive rate of the testing procedure
symbols.T_max: maximum expected sample usage per node

source.quote: Accuracy: For an arbitrary ε > 0, provided α, β ≤ (ε/D)^{1/⌈log D⌉} the probability of perfect recovery is P(A' = A) ≥ 1 − ε. Sample Complexity: Let Tmax be the maximum expected sample usage per node, and N be the sample complexity of the HDS algorithm. The expected sample complexity is bounded by: E(N) ≤ 2(1−α)/(1−2α) d⌈log D⌉Tmax

results.notes: Accuracy part: recovery probability ≥ 1−ε if α,β ≤ (ε/D)^{1/ceil(log D)}. Logs base 2.

bound.expression_latex: N < \bar N \equiv A d\lceil\log D\rceil(\log 16 + \frac{\log(1/\epsilon)}{\lceil \log D\rceil})

judicious choice of constants c_1, c_2

source.quote: Consider the HDS algorithm with non-sequential FDT using a fixed sample size per node A log(2/α)... Then, for a judicious choice of c1 and c2 the HDS-FDT procedure is correct with probability at least 1 − ε, and the sample complexity: N < N̄ ≡ A d⌈log D⌉(log 16 + log(1/ε)/⌈log D⌉).

results.notes: Paper's ε (failure probability) mapped to delta. Correct recovery w.p. ≥ 1−ε (probability over f and noise). Logs base 2. Text extracted from PDF, some formula details lossy.

source.quote: Running HDS with FDT and recovery rate 1 − ε, followed by the GP-UCB algorithm on the variables deemed active guarantees that with probability ≥ 1−δo: E(R_T) ≤ A'_T √T + (N̄ + 1)C0 + 2 + N̄C0/T. where A'_T = √(C1 βT γT) = O((log T)^{d/2+1}), C1 = 8/log(1 + b^{−2}), and N̄ = O(log(1/ε)^9) = O((log T)^9).
